newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids higher.

text.p: Dark Northern Spring wheat prices rose in line with the sharp runup in MGE spring wheat futures, dealers said.
Farm sales were brisk in parts of Montana and Minnesota, dealers said.

"We are starting to buy some new crop winter wheat at around 11.5 percent protein. I believe farmers want to get in there before it is all done and over it," a Montana merchandiser said, referring to Friday's sharp gains in wheat prices.

MGE May futures jumped 7-1/4 cents to $4.30 a bushel. MGE wheat futures closed higher on concerns about cold weather damage to the key-growing hard red winter wheat areas and on wet, cold weather that was delaying seeding of the spring wheat crop.
"The fields are too muddy. We still have snow on the ground," the Montana dealer said.

But flooding conditions in the Red River Valley area of North Dakota raised concerns about delays in spring wheat planting. Conditions there were at a standstill, a North Dakota dealer in the Red River region.
